In clinical quality registries, a **Quality Target** defines the specific performance threshold that healthcare departments are expected to achieve for a given medical indicator. These targets are critical for standardizing care, guiding quality improvement initiatives, and ensuring that evidence-based practices are consistently applied across hospitals.

Within the acute care and surgical database context, a key quality target has been established for [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]], which focuses on perioperative pain management and anesthetic protocols. The developmental goal for this indicator mandates that more than 60% of patients undergoing a [[laparotomi]] must receive an [[epidural]] [^src1]. This >60% threshold serves as a benchmark to evaluate whether surgical departments are adequately utilizing epidural analgesia—a practice often recommended to improve postoperative recovery and pain control in major open abdominal surgeries. Monitoring this target allows clinical teams to assess their adherence to established surgical pathways and identify gaps in perioperative care.
